name: Carlism
summary: Carlism is the Spanish traditionalist and legitimist movement, summed up as God, Fatherland, Fueros and King. It defends a hereditary Catholic monarchy limited by Church doctrine, law and traditional bodies, rejects national sovereignty and liberal parliamentary democracy, and upholds regional self-rule against centralization. It opposed both liberal capitalism and Marxism, favoring corporative Catholic social order.
scope: The historical mainstream traditionalist Carlism from Carlos VII through Vazquez de Mella and the Traditionalist Communion, up to the Franco era, based on the Morentin manifesto of 1874, Mella's doctrine and descriptions of the movement. It excludes the Carlos Hugo socialist turn of the 1960s-70s (Partido Carlista) and the Integrist and Francoist offshoots.

reification.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Carlism defends Church doctrine as binding and rejects liberal modernising of Catholic teaching.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religion is the cornerstone; the Marxist claim is rejected.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Ideario calls the Catholic religion "única verdadera", so authentic religions do not share one underlying truth.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Ideario requires laws and acts of government to conform to the principles taught by the Church's magisterium, so no other interpretation has equal legal standing.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

religious-nation.rationale: The Ideario says the Catholic religion has been "elemento determinante de nuestra nacionalidad, vínculo supremo de unidad de los pueblos hispánicos".

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Ideario says a king who departs from Dios, Patria, Fueros, Rey loses his sovereignty and "surge en el pueblo el derecho de rebeldía".

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Catholic teaching on property and the sources' defence of traditional property and corporative order point against equal common ownership.

restore-past-order.rationale: Carlism is counter-revolutionary and aims to restore Catholic traditional monarchy, though its motto speaks of defending in order to renew.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

right-to-secede.rationale: Carlism claims regional self-rule within a united Spain, a nested union of communities, not secession.

rule-by-example.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

sacred-nation.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The king is limited by Church and natural law, rather than divine himself.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Follows from the movement's Catholic social conservatism, with the family as the second level of its social order.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Catholic ethics and the social duties of rulers and wealthy contradict celebrating self-interest.

self-ownership.rationale: Catholic traditionalism limits individual autonomy by Church doctrine and the common good; sources stress authority and social duty.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Ideario says the state must "reverenciar públicamente a Dios como supremo Señor y Legislador y profesar la Religión Católica", with Church and state concording their relations.

separated-powers.rationale: The Ideario divides sovereignty into legislative, judicial and governing functions "independientes entre sí", with judges who settle disputes even with the king, though the functions are coordinated in the king.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Catholic natural-law thinking grounds human dignity in a God-given nature, and Carlists took firm stands such as opposition to abortion, so human nature is not seen as redesignable.

single-common-good.rationale: Catholic natural law and the king's duty to justice point to a common good known by reason.

single-official-language.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

social-market-economy.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Ideario says the king's power is limited by natural and divine law and that judges rule on disputes with the king, "sujeto a la ley igual que sus súbditos".

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

spiritual-nature.rationale: God and the Catholic Church are the first Carlist principle, and the movement held that politics must be ordered to man's religious end.

state-as-business.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

state-harmful.rationale: Carlism upholds a monarchy and public authority under God and law; Mella placed the state beneath society but never sought its abolition.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Carlism's creed is God, Fatherland, Fueros and King with Catholic unity as the basis of the state, so state promotion of atheism is the opposite of its programme.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: The Ideario says the state must conform laws and acts of government to natural and Christian principles and build structures that help men reach their supernatural end, and must preserve the people's religious belief against attacks.

strong-leader.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Ideario calls Church and state "sociedades perfectas y soberanas en sus respectivos órdenes", so the Church does not operate under the government's authority.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

taxation-theft.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Carlos VII's testament listed a Spanish Gibraltar and a new Moroccan empire among the aims of the "gran España tradicional", and Mella demanded sovereignty over the Strait.

total-state.rationale: Mella asserted society's superiority over the state and subsidiarity places authority at the lowest level.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Ideario sets the social sovereignty of tradition against the omnipotent state of democracy and of totalitarianism "de signo marxista o fascista", naming both alike.

traditional-family.rationale: The Ideario names marriage and family as the first associations, with a sphere of competence prior to the state.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Ideario says Spain's historical continuity is shown by a tradition that has defined its character "a través de los siglos".

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Fueros and regional law with unity without uniformity oppose a single civil law, and Catholic marriage law is distinct.

unions-good.rationale: Carlists founded the Catholic Sindicatos Libres in 1920 to balance workers' claims against upper-class interests, so unions are welcomed when Catholic and cooperative.

universal-morality.rationale: Carlists hold that God is Creator and Legislator, so natural moral law binds all.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Ideario limits the king's power by natural and divine laws "que no puede traspasar".

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its own rationale does not support its value under the reworded statement: it does not establish armed overthrow for failing to govern under religious law.

vanguard-party.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Traditionalist Catholic doctrine on the indissolubility of marriage excludes divorce at one spouse's request.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Carlism holds to Catholic doctrine, under which priestly and many teaching offices are reserved to men.

women-must-cover.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-18): the Ideario, the Aportes study of Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study state no position on this; the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and general doctrine, not a stated position.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Carlists preferred cooperation among classes through Catholic unions over democratic control.

missingStatements.text: Political authority ultimately comes from God rather than from the people.
missingStatements.rationale: Carlists reject national sovereignty and hold God to be Creator and Legislator, with the king bound by Church doctrine.

missingStatements.text: A country's constitution should reflect its historical traditions rather than abstract principles written by a legislature.
missingStatements.rationale: Carlists favored a historical constitution grounded in tradition and Catholic social teaching over a philosophical one.

missingStatements.text: A king who departs from the constitutional principles loses his sovereignty and the people gain a right of rebellion.
missingStatements.rationale: The Ideario states that if the king deviates from Dios, Patria, Fueros, Rey, he forfeits his sovereignty and the right of rebellion arises in the people.

missingStatements.text: The legislature should represent associations and corporations of society rather than political parties.
missingStatements.rationale: The Ideario says representation in the Cortes cannot be by parties but by territorial and institutional associations and corporations in which society organizes itself.

notes: Carlos Hugo's Partido Carlista (self-managed socialism) and Sixto Enrique's far-right line would answer very differently. Many answers are inferences because Carlist sources address mainly monarchy, religion, fueros and social order. Later pass (2026-11-18, rules 7): the party's own Ideario (CTC 2016), the Aportes article on Carlist foreign policy and the Tejada study were read for every statement; 96 earlier answers that rested on Wikipedia or on general doctrine were nulled, and the ones the Ideario, the Aportes study or the Tejada study state were re-sourced to them, each with its earlier version kept in reviewHistory. The 1874 Morentin manifesto (s3) is kept only in the histories: no saved source ties it to Carlism by name.
